images.title: Two scales for the fruit stall
images.purpose: Show the same fruit-stall data with two scales that both fit: 1 icon = 6 fruits needs 2, 3 and 5 icons, and 1 icon = 3 fruits needs 4, 6 and 10 icons.
images.composition: Two pictographs one above the other with the same round icon and the same rows, the top with the icon box 1 icon = 6 fruits and the bottom with the icon box 1 icon = 3 fruits.
images.exact_structure: Plain white frame, 1456 by 816, two pictographs of the same data, one above the other, split by one thin construction grey #6B7280 line (3 px) at y 408 from x 60 to x 1396. In both, every row name (Apples, Oranges, Bananas) is left-aligned at x 100 in dark #1F2937 bold sans-serif (38 px) and centred on its row, and every icon is the same plain round icon: a teal #0072B2 circle 60 px across with a thin dark #2B2B2B outline (3 px), the icons of a row in one line with their centres 72 px apart, the first centre at x 360. TOP PICTOGRAPH: an icon box (white rounded rectangle, corner radius 16, dark outline 4 px) x 1060 to 1400, y 30 to 100, holding the text 1 icon = 6 fruits centred at (1230, 65), dark #1F2937 bold (36 px). Three rows centred on y 160, 250 and 340: Apples with exactly 2 icons (centres x 360 and 432), Oranges with exactly 3 icons (centres x 360, 432 and 504), Bananas with exactly 5 icons (centres x 360, 432, 504, 576 and 648). BOTTOM PICTOGRAPH: an icon box x 1060 to 1400, y 430 to 500, holding the text 1 icon = 3 fruits centred at (1230, 465), same style. Three rows centred on y 560, 650 and 740: Apples with exactly 4 icons (centres x 360, 432, 504 and 576), Oranges with exactly 6 icons (centres x 360 to 720, one every 72 px), Bananas with exactly 10 icons (centres x 360 to 1008, one every 72 px, the last icon ending at x 1038). No number is written at the end of a row. In all there are 10 icons in the top pictograph, 20 icons in the bottom one and 30 icons in the frame. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
a different number of icons from 2, 3, 5 above and 4, 6, 10 below, or an icon of another shape in one of the pictographs
a number written at the end of any row, or any part or half of an icon
an icon box that gives a scale other than 6 fruits for the top and 3 fruits for the bottom
images.takeaway: The same data can be shown with different scales that fit every number; a smaller scale needs more icons.
images.description: Two pictographs of 12 apples, 18 oranges and 30 bananas: with 1 icon = 6 fruits the rows have 2, 3 and 5 icons, and with 1 icon = 3 fruits they have 4, 6 and 10 icons.
images.context: Concept image for Choosing a Different Scale. It follows the idea of the book's pictographs with an icon box and uses the numbers of this concept's own example: 12 apples, 18 oranges and 30 bananas with the scales 6 and 3.
images.teaching_notes: Let the student compare the two bottom and top rows: the rows are twice as long when the scale is half as big. The slip to watch: thinking a bigger scale needs more icons.

image_decisions.why: The same fruit data drawn with two scales one above the other shows that both fit and that the smaller scale needs more icons.
